claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic alloy with a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
The incoherent interfaces concentrate stress and cause brittleness.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the lamellar microstructure into a hierarchical pattern.
The HPHT treatment will replace incoherent FCC/B2 boundaries with coherent interfaces.
A hexahedron-anvil apparatus can impose the proposed HPHT treatment on this alloy.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between the two phases.
The transformed structure will activate dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning as concurrent deformation mechanisms.
Dislocation transfer through coherent interfaces will produce a more homogeneous strain distribution.
The homogeneous strain distribution will arrest interfacial cracking.
After treatment, the GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain.
The treated sample will show elongated crack propagation rather than isolated microcracks.
The HPHT-treated alloy will have significantly improved ductility without sacrificing strength.
Approximately 6 GPa is sufficient to induce the required topological transformation.
A temperature of 1473 K is sufficient for atomic rearrangement while remaining below the phase-instability or melting threshold.
Exceeding the FCC/B2 stability limits could cause phase decomposition or melting.
Conventional thermal-mechanical treatments fail to produce the proposed hierarchical interface coherence.
Deformation mechanisms are extrapolated from Ag and CoNiCrFeMn systems rather than demonstrated in HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
High pressure can alter interface energetics in a way that promotes the proposed coherent hierarchical topology.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says interfacial cracking will be arrested, whereas the predicted outcome explicitly expects elongated crack propagation. Without explaining why elongated cracks indicate improvement, these descriptions point in opposing directions.
